system_note:
What was billed: Principal M72.6 (Necrotizing fasciitis) [POA=Y, MCC], plus R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) [POA=Y, MCC], organism lines A49.59 / A49.02 / B95.62, J96.01/J80 for respiratory failure/ARDS, multiple diabetes codes, AKI (N17.9), and procedures including emergent debridement, ETT insertion, prolonged ventilation, PICC/central line insertion, and a billed 0HRJX73 (replacement of right upper leg skin with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness). What the record documents (key citations): H&P and ED/consult notes document CT-confirmed necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh with palpable crepitus and emergent operative management (History & Physical; Emergency Dept note; General Surgery consult): CT scan confirmed necrotizing fasciitis of the right thigh, and emergent surgical consultation was obtained (History & Physical, p.295) [ev_0001]; Type II necrotizing soft-tissue infection with rapid progression, hemodynamic instability, and radiographic gas in the soft tissues (General Surgery Consult, p.379) ; and the ICU/attending notes state emergent surgical debridement was performed with extensive tissue removal to fascia and that the patient had septic shock requiring vasopressors and was intubated for respiratory failure (Critical Care Progress Note, p.216) [ev_0002]. Deep tissue cultures identified Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (Infectious Diseases consult, p.172). The discharge summary documents multiple debridements and a split-thickness skin graft (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.979) [ev_0003]. What the governing policies require (key citations): Coding M72.6 (necrotizing fasciitis, MCC) requires provider documentation of confirmed necrotizing fasciitis plus operative or imaging confirmation of fascial-plane involvement or the presumption rules for transferred operative confirmation (Necrotizing Fasciitis policy - Validation Criteria: Criterion 1 requires provider documentation of 'necrotizing fasciitis' in operative or attending/ID notes; Criterion 3 requires at least one operative finding such as gross fascial necrosis) [pol_001, pol_002]. The Sepsis policy requires that severe sepsis / septic shock (R65.21) be supported by documentation of septic shock (vasopressor use + lactate criteria or explicit physician documentation of septic shock) and, when an organism is identified, that the appropriate organism-specific sepsis code (A40.- or A41.-) be assigned (Sepsis policy: vasopressor documentation and lactate criteria; and organism → A40/A41 mapping) [pol_003, pol_004, pol_005, pol_006]. Assessment tying record to policy and findings:
- Necrotizing fasciitis (M72.6): Supported. CT imaging showing gas in fascial planes and operative debridement with tissue removal to fascia meet the policy's Validation Criteria (operative confirmation or imaging) for M72.6. Evidence: CT-confirmation and emergent operative debridement (History & Physical p.295 [ev_0001]; General Surgery consult p.379 ; Critical Care Progress Note p.216 [ev_0002]; Necrotizing Fasciitis policy requirements [pol_001, pol_002]). Keep M72.6 as an MCC-level diagnosis and POA=Y is supported by documentation that these findings were present on initial presentation. - Severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21): Supported clinically (documented septic shock with vasopressors and elevated lactate in progress notes: see Critical Care Progress Note showing vasopressors and ABG/lactate and P/F ratio consistent with organ dysfunction) and appropriately MCC-level under policy [ev_0002; pol_003; pol_004]. R65.21 as an additional diagnosis is supported, POA=Y is consistent with documentation of shock on admission. - Organism coding / sequencing error (Finding): The medical record documents identified organisms (deep tissue cultures grew Streptococcus pyogenes [Group A] and MRSA). The Sepsis policy explicitly maps identified organisms to organism-specific sepsis codes (e.g., Group A Streptococcus → A40.0; Staphylococcus aureus - MRSA → A41.02) and instructs coders to use A40.- / A41.- when the organism is identified rather than A49.- / B95.x organism/unspecified-site codes alone [pol_005, pol_006]. This claim instead lists A49.59 / A49.02 and B95.62 while also coding R65.21. That combination does not follow the policy pathway for documented sepsis with identified organism: when an organism causing sepsis is identified, the appropriate A40.- or A41.- sepsis code should be assigned (and R65.21 reported as additional), rather than A49.- / B95.x organism codes alone. Therefore the organism/sepsis coding is misclassified and must be corrected (remove A49.59 / A49.02 / B95.62 and substitute A40.0 [sepsis due to Group A Streptococcus]; this added A40.0 will be flagged for reviewer confirmation given polymicrobial cultures) Evidence: cultures positive for Group A Strep and MRSA (Infectious Diseases consult p.172) ; policy mapping (Group A → A40.0; MRSA → A41.02) [pol_005, pol_006]. - Procedure technique mismatch (Finding): The discharge and procedure documentation document a split-thickness skin graft (STSG) on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take (Discharge / Transfer Summary, p.979) [ev_0003], while the billed PCS 0HRJX73 describes replacement with an autologous tissue substitute, full thickness. The record supports a split-thickness graft rather than a full-thickness autologous tissue substitute as billed; coding should be changed to the correct PCS for a split-thickness skin graft (or removed/recoded) — physician/coding clarification required. Evidence: discharge summary documents split-thickness skin graft (p.979) [ev_0003]. Other diagnoses and procedures (respiratory failure, ARDS, AKI, DKA, prolonged ventilation, central line/PICC, platelet transfusion, diabetes comorbidities): clinically supported by H&P, ICU notes, nephrology and ID consults and discharge summary (examples: severe DKA pH 6.98 [History & Physical, p.295] ; ABG/lactate and P/F ratio consistent with respiratory failure/ARDS [Critical Care Progress Note, p.216] ; nephrology consult documenting AKI peak and conservative management [NOTE n43]; discharge summary documenting course and recovery) and may be kept as billed. The prolonged ventilation/procedure 5A1D90Z is supported by early intubation for respiratory failure, ARDS, and extended ICU course (intubation on admission + ARDS and very low P/F) though the precise >96-hour documentation that coders require should be verified in ICU flow sheets; we cite the sustained ARDS/intubation and long ICU stay as clinical support (Critical Care Progress Note p.216; Discharge Summary p.979) [ev_0002, ev_0003]. Summary of changes required (high-level):
1) Remove the non-sepsis organism codes (A49.59, A49.02, B95.62) and replace with the organism-specific sepsis code A40.0 (sepsis due to Group A Streptococcus); this added A40.0 will be flagged for reviewer confirmation given polymicrobial cultures (evidence: culture results and policy mapping) [pol_005, pol_006].
2) Clarify principal-diagnosis sequencing (whether principal should remain M72.6 or whether organism-specific sepsis [A40.- / A41.-] should be sequenced principal with R65.21 as additional? Please confirm intended sequencing per physician documentation). The record supports M72.6 as the operative, source-control diagnosis, but Sepsis policy favors A40/A41 pairing with R65.21 when sepsis is the primary reason for admission; this sequencing decision requires coder/physician clarification.
3) Remove or recode PCS 0HRJX73 (billed as full-thickness autologous tissue replacement) because the record documents a split-thickness skin graft (Discharge Summary p.979) [ev_0003]; replace with the correct PCS for split-thickness graft after physician/operative note confirmation. Evidence cited (by id): ev_0001, ev_0002, pol_001, pol_002, pol_003, pol_004, pol_005, pol_006, ev_0003. Determination: Finding — because the organism/sepsis coding does not follow the Sepsis policy (identified organism(s) present → use A40.-/A41.- sepsis codes with R65.21) and the billed skin-replacement PCS (0HRJX73) conflicts with the operative/discharge documentation documenting a split-thickness skin graft. Recommended corrective actions and specific coder/physician queries are provided in the rationale letter and in the HITL question below.
rationale_letter:
Dear Provider/Coding Team, Re: MR_05 (Admit 02/19/2026–Discharge/Transfer 06/06/2026) — Audit Finding: Sepsis/organism coding and one procedure technique mismatch We reviewed the full inpatient record (History & Physical, Critical Care notes, General Surgery consult, Infectious Diseases consult, and Discharge/Transfer Summary) against our DRG coding policies. The audit identified two issues that require correction: 1) Sepsis/organism coding does not follow policy for documented organism-specific sepsis.
Basis: Deep tissue cultures identified Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (Infectious Diseases consult, 02/21/2026). Our Sepsis policy requires that when a causative organism is identified for sepsis, an organism-specific sepsis code from A40.- or A41.- is assigned (examples: Group A Streptococcus -> A40.0; MRSA -> A41.02) and R65.21 (severe sepsis with septic shock) is coded as an additional code per policy mapping [pol_005, pol_006]. The claim billed A49.59 / A49.02 and B95.62 for the organisms while also billing R65.21. Per policy, the appropriate action when cultures identify the sepsis organism is to assign the organism-specific sepsis code (A40.- / A41.-) rather than non-sepsis organism-site codes alone. Therefore we are removing A49.59 / A49.02 / B95.62 and will add A40.0 (sepsis due to Group A Streptococcus) paired with R65.21; this added A40.0 will be flagged for reviewer confirmation given the polymicrobial cultures (see HITL question below). 2) Procedure technique mismatch — skin graft type:
Basis: The discharge summary documents a split-thickness skin graft on ICU day 18 with excellent graft take (Discharge / Transfer Summary, 06/06/2026) [ev_0003]. The billed PCS 0HRJX73 describes replacement of right upper leg skin with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness. The clinical documentation supports a split-thickness skin graft (STSG), not a full-thickness autologous replacement as billed; this requires recoding to the correct ICD-10-PCS code for STSG or removal/replacement depending on the operative note. Please provide the operative report that documents the graft thickness and technique so coding may be corrected. What we are changing now (audit correction to be applied unless provider supplies clarifying documentation within the appeal period):
- Remove A49.59 (other streptococcal infection), A49.02 (MRSA infection, unspecified site), and B95.62 (MRSA as cause of disease elsewhere) and add A40.0 (sepsis due to Group A Streptococcus) paired with R65.21; the added A40.0 is flagged for reviewer confirmation given that cultures also grew MRSA (evidence: deep tissue cultures positive for Group A Strep and MRSA [ID consult] and policy organism mapping [pol_005, pol_006]).
- Remove procedure 0HRJX73 (replacement with autologous tissue substitute, full thickness) and recode to the appropriate PCS reflecting a split-thickness skin graft after review of the operative report/skin-graft operative note (Discharge summary documents STSG on ICU day 18) [ev_0003]. Requested documentation to resolve outstanding items (please supply within 30 days):
1. Operative report(s) for the index debridement(s) and the skin graft procedure that document whether the graft was split-thickness versus full-thickness and the exact graft technique/materials used. (Needed to assign correct PCS code in place of 0HRJX73.)
2. Clarification from the operative/surgical or infectious disease team as to which organism should be coded as the organism responsible for sepsis when multiple organisms grew (Group A Streptococcus vs MRSA), or documentation that sepsis was polymicrobial and how you want it reflected in coded sepsis (A40.0 vs A41.02 vs combination). This will determine whether A40.0 or A41.02 (or both) should be used and whether sepsis should be sequenced principal vs secondary. If no additional documentation is provided, the claim-level corrections described above will be applied: remove A49.59/A49.02/B95.62; add A40.0 (sepsis due to Group A Streptococcus) paired with R65.21 (A40.0 flagged for reviewer confirmation); remove 0HRJX73 and recode OR mark for recoding pending operative report. Sincerely,
Clinical Claims Audit Team Key evidence cited: History & Physical (admit H&P) and surgical/ICU notes documenting CT and operative debridement of necrotizing fasciitis [ev_0001, ev_0002]; Infectious Diseases consult documenting Group A Streptococcus and MRSA growth ; Necrotizing Fasciitis policy Validation Criteria (operative confirmation requirement) [pol_001, pol_002]; Sepsis policy vasopressor/lactate and organism-to-sepsis-code mapping (A40.0 / A41.02) [pol_003, pol_004, pol_005, pol_006]; Discharge summary documenting STSG [ev_0003].
